channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Virginia moves to forbid schools from teaching Jan. 6 was peaceful
item.description: Virginia lawmakers passed a bill prohibiting schools from teaching that Jan. 6 was peaceful or that 2020 election fraud was widespread, marking a first for a Democratic state.

item.title: Negligence – Ransomware attack – Economic loss doctrine
item.description: Where negligence claims have been brought by a plaintiff that suffered a ransomware attack that resulted in the deletion of its stored electronic data until it paid the requested ransom, a motion to dismiss those claims should be denied because the plaintiff’s complete loss of electronic data is sufficiently tangible to qualify as property damage so as to avoid the economic loss doctrine.

item.title: Superior Court reverses CRAB’s denial of accidental death benefits
item.description: A Superior Court judge reinstated accidental death benefits for a state employee killed in a car accident while performing work duties, reversing CRAB's decision.

item.title: Jury: State Police trooper suffered gender-based bias
item.description: The plaintiff sued the State Police and a fellow trooper after a series of investigations stemming from her discovery in 2016 of sexually explicit material stored on a personal hard drive the fellow trooper had connected to a State Police computer.

item.title: The fix is in
item.description: Henry Hill revealed a 1978 scheme by the Lucchese crime family to fix Boston College basketball games, involving players, gamblers, and mob bosses.

item.title: SCOTUS: State-created transit corp. not immune from PI suits
item.description: U.S. Supreme Court rules New Jersey Transit is not entitled to sovereign immunity, allowing negligence lawsuits over bus accidents in New York and Pennsylvania.

item.title: AG Campbell passes on ‘inadequate’ settlement with ticketing giant
item.description: Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea J. Campbell calls the DOJ's settlement with Live Nation 'inadequate' and continues her antitrust lawsuit over Ticketmaster's market dominance.

item.title: ‘Not a federal offense’: Defense seeks dismissal in Birchmore case
item.description: Matthew Farwell's defense challenges federal jurisdiction in Boston case, arguing charges related to killing Sandra Birchmore do not meet federal statute requirements.

item.title: Ex-Quincy official pleads guilty to stealing from senior center
item.description: Tom Clasby, former Quincy elder services director, pleaded guilty to stealing over $144,000 from the senior center between 2020 and 2024.

item.title: Trump administration seeks to revive executive orders targeting law firms
item.description: The Trump administration seeks to revive executive orders targeting four major U.S. law firms, arguing federal judges exceeded their authority in blocking the directives.
